en.title: Xbox's Doom and Wolfenstein Studios Deepen Ties Post-Layoffs
en.summary: id Software and MachineGames are collaborating more than ever, signaling a new era for Bethesda's flagship shooter franchises. This intensified partnership follows recent layoffs at id Software.
en.body:
Following a period of significant restructuring within Xbox's gaming divisions, **id Software** and **MachineGames**, two of the most celebrated first-person shooter developers under the Bethesda umbrella, are reportedly working together more closely than ever before. This announcement comes from **id Software** co-director **Marty Stratton**, who addressed the studio's status in the wake of recent layoffs that impacted roughly half of its staff as part of Xbox CEO **Asha Sharma**'s broader company "reset."

Despite the challenging circumstances, Stratton emphasized the studio's resilience and forward momentum. "We're doing great," he stated at a recent press event for **Doom: The Dark Ages**'s Revelations DLC. "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away...everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department." He elaborated on the deepening relationship with **MachineGames**, creators of the recent **Wolfenstein** titles and the upcoming **Indiana Jones and the Great Circle**. "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever. We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead."

## A Shared Future for Iconic Franchises

This intensified collaboration is particularly significant given the historical synergy between the two studios. **MachineGames** has consistently utilized **id Software**'s proprietary **idTech** engine for all its **Wolfenstein** titles, a testament to the robust and adaptable technology **id Software** has developed over decades. The timing of this closer working relationship also aligns with **Xbox CEO Asha Sharma**'s stated vision for her studios to "double down on their biggest franchises." This suggests a strategic push to leverage the established strengths and fan bases of franchises like **Doom** and **Wolfenstein**.

While **Marty Stratton** did not explicitly confirm any joint projects, the implications are tantalizing for fans. The possibility of **id Software** and **MachineGames** co-developing future titles, perhaps even the heavily rumored **Wolfenstein 3**, is a compelling prospect. **MachineGames** studio head **Jerk Gustafsson** has previously stated, "We're not done with **Wolfenstein** yet," fueling speculation that the beloved alternate-history shooter series is far from over. This deepened technological and creative partnership could lead to groundbreaking advancements in both franchises, blending **id Software**'s legendary shooter pedigree with **MachineGames**'s narrative-driven approach.

## What's Next

Fans eager for new content from these studios can anticipate further developments regarding **Doom: The Dark Ages** and **Indiana Jones and the Great Circle**. While specific details on any potential co-developed projects are not yet public, the renewed focus and collaboration between **id Software** and **MachineGames** suggest a strong pipeline of high-quality, franchise-focused titles for Xbox and PC players in the coming years.

content_raw: Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. At a press event earlier this week for id Software's Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which was released this summer, studio co-director Marty Stratton was asked how the studio is doing in the wake of the layoffs that affected id as part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's ongoing Xbox " reset ." He answered, "We're doing great. Not to handwave the [layoffs] away...everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department. "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever. We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead." This is purely speculative on my part, but might the two decorated first-person shooter studios be co-developing MachineGames's next project, which is heavily rumored to be Wolfenstein 3 – with studio head Jerk Gustafsson saying, "We're not done with Wolfenstein yet"? Not only has MachineGames used id Software's idTech engine for every one of its games, but Sharma has publicly stated that she wants Xbox's development teams to double down on their biggest franchises – a sentiment echoed by Bethesda boss Jill Braff. And with id now seemingly done with Doom: The Dark Ages following the oustanding Revelations DLC, a team-up with MachineGames might help get the rumored third Wolfenstein game out the door faster, and getting games out more quickly is one of Sharma's goals. In addition, while Doom should certainly be considered in that "biggest franchises" group, Wolfenstein most likely is as well. Plus, Amazon has a Wolfenstein TV series in development, which might further incentivize Xbox and Bethesda to pair up id and MachineGames to make sure the latter team's next game is as awesome – and out as quickly – as possible. Bu whatever either team does next, the project(s) will be highly anticipated, at least by me, as both teams have incredible track records, both historically and recently.
